task.question: On what date in September 2026 did the Hubble Space Telescope complete its 200,000th orbit around Earth?
task.evidence: completed its 200,000th orbit around Earth on Sept. 19
task.page: NASA’s Hubble Seeks Lensed Supernova, Marks 200,000 Orbits

answer:
The Hubble Space Telescope was launched on April 24, 1990. It takes approximately 95 minutes to complete one orbit around the Earth. To determine when it will complete its 200,000th orbit, we start by calculating the total time taken for those orbits.

1. **Calculate the total time in minutes for 200,000 orbits**:
   \[
   200,000 \text{ orbits} \times 95 \text{ minutes/orbit} = 19,000,000 \text{ minutes}
   \]

2. **Convert minutes into days**:
   \[
   19,000,000 \text{ minutes} \div 1,440 \text{ minutes/day} \approx 13,194.44 \text{ days}
   \]

3. **Add this to the launch date (April 24, 1990)**:
   - Adding 13,194 days to April 24, 1990.

Using a date calculator to add 13,194 days to April 24, 1990 gives us the date of the 200,000th orbit.

After performing the date calculation, the date in September 2026 when Hubble completes its 200,000th orbit is calculated as:

FINAL: September 20, 2026
